feed.title: Practice & Challenges — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: An annotated directory of links on software, AI, security and science. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Awesome Code Review
entry.summary: A resource list for the practice and tools of code review.

entry.title: Beecrowd
entry.summary: An online judge grading programming, mathematics and SQL problems automatically.

entry.title: Code Golf (Stack Exchange)
entry.summary: A community contest to solve a problem in the shortest possible code.

entry.title: CodePen Challenges
entry.summary: Front-end (HTML/CSS/JS) challenges with an embedded editor.

entry.title: Daily Coding Problem
entry.summary: A service that emails one coding-interview problem every day.

entry.title: devChallenges.io
entry.summary: A challenge site that has you build web projects with realistic designs and requirements. Unlike random projects the community reviews the solutions.

entry.title: GeeksforGeeks
entry.summary: A very broad article archive of algorithms, data structures and interview questions. Unlike single-topic sites it has a worked example for almost every CS topic.

entry.title: Project Euler Archives
entry.summary: An archived collection of problems joining mathematics and programming.

entry.title: RealWorld
entry.summary: A spec whose same realistic app (Conduit) is built across different front-end and back-end stacks.

entry.title: Rosetta Code
entry.summary: A wiki showing the same small problem solved in hundreds of languages. Unlike single-language examples it shows side by side how a task differs across languages.

entry.title: TodoMVC
entry.summary: Shows the same to-do app built in dozens of JavaScript frameworks so you can compare them side by side.

entry.title: TopCoder Arena
entry.summary: The classic arena for timed algorithm competitions (SRM).

entry.title: UVa Online Judge
entry.summary: A classic online judge auto-grading hundreds of contest problems.

entry.title: Python Tutor
entry.summary: Steps through code drawing stack frames and heap objects. Nothing explains reference semantics, scope and mutable default arguments as clearly.

entry.title: AlgoDS
entry.summary: Java implementations of algorithms and data structures, each written readably and with tests.

entry.title: Algorithm Design Canvas
entry.summary: A stepwise framework for approaching an interview algorithm problem — constraints, examples, brute force, optimise, test. Method instead of panic.

entry.title: AtCoder
entry.summary: A Japan-based contest platform whose beginner rounds (ABC) are more approachable for newcomers than Codeforces.

entry.title: Big-O Cheat Sheet
entry.summary: A single colour-coded table of time and space complexity for data structures and sorting algorithms — the last look before an interview.

entry.title: Big-O Yanılgıları
entry.summary: A piece correcting common misunderstandings of big-O notation, such as conflating worst case with average case.

entry.title: Bit İşlemleri Numaraları
entry.summary: A collection of common bit-level tricks — the patterns that turn up in low-level optimisation and interview questions.

entry.title: CodeAbbey
entry.summary: A problem sequence starting at the very easiest and climbing gradually — a far gentler curve than the contest platforms for absolute beginners.

entry.title: CodeChef
entry.summary: A competitive algorithm platform with monthly contests, difficulty-tagged problems and published editorial solutions.

entry.title: Codeforces
entry.summary: The busiest competitive programming platform, with regular rounds and a rating system. Problems run harder than LeetCode and lean heavily mathematical.

entry.title: CodeGym
entry.summary: A practice-heavy course teaching Java through 1,200 hands-on tasks.

entry.title: Coderbyte
entry.summary: An interview problem bank and assessment tool with video explanations of solutions.

entry.title: CodeSignal
entry.summary: A skills assessment and interview platform that produces a standardised score you can send to several companies. The single assessment is the difference from sitting a separate test for every employer.

entry.title: Codility
entry.summary: The assessment platform companies use for technical screening, with a practice section open to candidates. Its difference from other problem sites is that it mirrors the format of real screening tests — you see the exam environment before the exam.

entry.title: CodinGame
entry.summary: A platform that has you solve programming puzzles with a game theme, showing your code’s result in a game scene. Unlike dry problem sets it animates your solution visually.

entry.title: Competitive Programmer’s Handbook
entry.summary: A free handbook for competitive programming, from basic algorithms to advanced techniques. Against academic algorithm books it is contest-oriented: it hands you an implementable template rather than a proof.

entry.title: CryptoHack
entry.summary: Teaches cryptography by breaking it, with each level exploiting a real weakness — the applied counterpart to a theory course.

entry.title: freeCodeCamp
entry.summary: A complete free curriculum with in-browser exercises and free certificates. Its capstone projects make you build real applications rather than stopping at drills.

entry.title: Glitch
entry.summary: A browser environment for small apps that go live instantly — for testing an idea while skipping setup and deployment entirely.

entry.title: Google Interview Warmup
entry.summary: A practice tool where you answer interview questions aloud and get AI feedback.

entry.title: HackerEarth
entry.summary: Combines contests with hiring assessments — companies run technical screening here.

entry.title: HiredInTech
entry.summary: Structured courses for system-design and algorithm interviews.

entry.title: InterviewBit
entry.summary: Gamified interview preparation ordered by topic dependency, each subject building on the last.

entry.title: InterviewThis
entry.summary: A list of questions to ask the company in an interview — it flips the direction so you can assess the workplace.

entry.title: Learnersbucket
entry.summary: A practice archive focused on JavaScript interview questions: writing polyfills, the event loop, closures. Unlike general algorithm sites it is language-specific — "implement bind yourself" is not a question you find elsewhere.

entry.title: mission-peace/interview
entry.summary: A large collection of coding-interview problems and solutions, with video explanations.

entry.title: NeetCode
entry.summary: A roadmap that groups LeetCode problems by topic and pairs each with a solution video. Against a raw problem list the difference is ordering: which 150 problems, in which sequence, teach the patterns — the thing random grinding never gives you.
